cards.title: Geometric patterns

Each exterior of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two interior opposites. Sum of one exterior at each vertex of any convex polygon = 360°.

cards.title: More notes
body: Always name the arc when you claim “angle at the centre is twice…”. Wrong arc is the standard error. For polygons, interior + adjacent exterior = 180° if the exterior is the extension of one side.

cards.title: 3.1.1 Polygons
body: Polygons could be classified according to the number of sides they have.
Polygons of sides 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12 could also be given special names.
Regular polygons are polygons with all angles equal and all sides of the same length.Regular polygons are both equiangular and equilateral.
An equilateral triangle is always equiangular.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a 15-sided polygon?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write down the interior angle sum formula**
The sum of the interior angles $$S$$ of an $$n$$-sided polygon is:
$$S = (n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$$

**Step 2: Substitute $$n = 15$$ into the formula**
$$S = (15 - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$$
$$S = 13 \times 180^{\circ}$$

**Step 3: Perform the multiplication**
$$S = 2340^{\circ}$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The sum of the interior angles is **$$2340^{\circ}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Calculate the measure of each interior angle of a regular octagon.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write down the formula for one interior angle**
For a regular polygon with $$n$$ sides, each interior angle is:
$$\text{Angle} = \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}}{n}$$

**Step 2: Substitute $$n = 8$$ for an octagon**
$$\text{Angle} = \frac{(8 - 2) \times 180^{\circ}}{8}$$
$$\text{Angle} = \frac{6 \times 180^{\circ}}{8}$$
$$\text{Angle} = \frac{1080^{\circ}}{8}$$

**Step 3: Simplify the fraction**
$$\text{Angle} = 135^{\circ}$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
Each interior angle of a regular octagon is **$$135^{\circ}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If the sum of the interior angles of a polygon is $$2160^{\circ}$$, how many sides does the polygon have?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Set up the equation using the sum formula**
$$(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = 2160^{\circ}$$

**Step 2: Solve for $$(n - 2)$$**
Divide both sides by $$180^{\circ}$$:
$$n - 2 = \frac{2160}{180}$$
$$n - 2 = 12$$

**Step 3: Solve for $$n$$**
$$n = 12 + 2$$
$$n = 14$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The polygon has **$$14$$** sides.

lessons.title: Angles and Arc Relationship of Circles

cards.title: Angles and Arc Relationship of Circles
body: Circle: angle in a semicircle = 90°. Angle at the centre = twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc. Angles in the same segment are equal. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. Tangent ⊥ radius. Two tangents from an external point are equal.

cards.title: Circle pack
body: Same arc → same circumference angle. Centre is the greedy double. Cyclic opposite = 180°. Tangent and radius shake hands at 90°.

cards.title: 3.2.1 Angles in a Circle
body: **Chord** is a line segment joining any two points of a circle.
A chord that passes through the centre of a circle is called a **diameter**.
In a circle with radius 5 cm, two chords AB and CD have lengths 4 cm and 6 cm, respectively.
Theorem 3.5: If a central angle and an inscribed angle of a circle are subtended on the same arc, then the inscribed angle is half of the central angle.

cards.title: 3.2.2 Cyclic Quadrilateral
body: Repeat the process for other circles with different radii.
A quadrilateral whose vertices lie on a circle or which is inscribed in a circle is called a **cyclic quadrilateral**.
Theorem 3.7: The measure of the angle formed by two lines intersecting inside a circle is half the sum of the measures of the arcs subtending the angle and its vertical opposite.

cards.title: 3.2.3 Properties of Tangents in Circles
body: The point at which the tangent intersects is called the point of tangency or the point of contact.
Arcs intercepted by parallel chords are congruent.

cards.title: Worked example: angles in a circle
cards.problem: O is the centre of a circle. A, B, C, D lie on the circle with ABCD a cyclic quadrilateral. The central angle on the minor arc AC is ∠AOC = 140°, B lies on the major arc and D on the minor arc. Find ∠ABC and ∠ADC.

steps.text: Step 1: the angle at the circumference on the same arc is half the central angle. If B is on the major arc, ∠ABC = ½ × 140° = 70°.
Step 2: ABCD is cyclic, so opposite angles are supplementary: ∠ADC = 180° − 70° = 110°.
Step 3: check: D is on the minor arc, and its angle uses the reflex central angle 360° − 140° = 220°, half of which is 110° ✔.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: The angle at the centre of a circle on arc PQ is 96°. What is the angle at the circumference on the same arc?
cards.why: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc, so the circumference angle is 96° ÷ 2 = 48°.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, ∠P = 75°. What is ∠R?
cards.why: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°: ∠R = 180° − 75° = 105°.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: AB is a diameter and C is any other point on the circle. What is ∠ACB?
cards.why: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle: the central angle on the diameter is 180°, and half of it is 90°, wherever C is.

cards.title: Secants, Tangent and Chords: Properties
body: A **chord** joins two points of a circle; a **secant** is a line that cuts the circle at two points; a **tangent** touches it at exactly one point and is perpendicular to the radius there.
**Two chords intersecting inside** at E (chords AB and CD): AE × EB = CE × ED. Angle between them: ∠AEC = ½(arc AC + arc BD).
**Two secants from an outside point P** (PAB and PCD, with A and C nearer): PA × PB = PC × PD (outer part × whole secant).
**Tangent and secant from P** (tangent PT, secant PAB): PT² = PA × PB.
**Two tangents from P** are equal: PT₁ = PT₂.
**Example:** from P, a secant meets the circle at A and B with PA = 4 cm and AB = 5 cm, so PB = 9 cm. The tangent PT satisfies PT² = 4 × 9 = 36, so PT = 6 cm.

cards.title: 3.3.1 Lines intersecting Inside the Circle
body: If two chords TQ and RS, intersect at E, then TE × EQ = RE × ES.

cards.title: 3.3.3 Chords Intersecting Outside of a Circle
body: The angles of a quadrilateral are related so that the second is twice the first, the third is three times the first, and the fourth is four times the first.
If m(arc ABC) = 2x + 110 and m(arc DEF) = x + 100, find the value of x.
Two secants AB and CD of a circle with centre O intersect outside of the circle at K.

cards.title: Worked example: intersecting chords
cards.problem: Chords AB and CD meet at E inside a circle. AE = 6 cm, EB = 4 cm and CE = 3 cm. Find ED and the length of CD.

steps.text: Step 1: intersecting chords theorem: AE × EB = CE × ED.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: From an external point P, a tangent PT = 8 cm and a secant PAB with PA = 4 cm. Find PB.
cards.why: Tangent–secant theorem: PT² = PA × PB → 64 = 4 × PB → PB = 16 cm.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: Two secants from P: PA = 3, PB = 12 and PC = 4. Find PD.
cards.why: PA × PB = PC × PD → 3 × 12 = 4 × PD → PD = 9.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: A tangent meets a radius at the point of contact. The angle between them is…
cards.why: A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact.
